weaknesses: The paper calls its explicit procedure attaining, but never says that its polynomial and pilot branches only switch on when L=log(ed)≥4096, that is d≥e^{4095}. For every dimension a practitioner could meet, \cref{obj:def:frontier-handle} reduces to the plug-in average of |W̄_j|, a constant fallback, or the constant 1/2. The interval radius q_*=√(10^{17}ρ) also clips to the trivial interval [1/4,3/4] unless ρ<10^{-18}. Fix: state these thresholds in the main text right after the construction (\cref{obj:def:frontier-handle} and the discussion after \cref{obj:thm:uniform-private-value-frontiers}). Present the procedure as a device for establishing the rate, with constants chosen for the proof. Move the practical-constants discussion into the Limitations section, and consider a remark on what the procedure does for moderate d.

The assumption discussion is out of step with the assumptions it sits next to, and it is mostly decorative citation. In Section 3.1 each commentary paragraph describes the previous environment, not the adjacent one. Examples: text about uniform sampling follows the fair-randomization assumption; text about consistency follows the interior-means assumption; text about interior means follows the iid assumption. Restrictiveness is never weighed. Uniform public stratum probabilities, an exact 1/2 propensity conditional on potential outcomes, and means confined to [1/4,3/4] are strong, and the paper does not ask which of them are needed for the rate or which are conveniences. Fix: place each motivation paragraph directly after its assumption. Add a short paragraph saying which conclusions survive known non-uniform strata or known propensity bounded away from 0 and 1, and what the interior-means restriction buys (b>d, bounded contrasts).

The positioning omits the closest nonsmooth-functional precedents and leans on loosely described recent working papers. Missing: Lepski, Nemirovski and Spokoiny (1999) on estimating L_r norms, which gives the log-type rates for ℓ1-norm estimation; Polyanskiy–Wu and Jiao–Han-type results on polynomial approximation for L1 distance (cited only for the direct-sample setting); and private ℓ1-distance and identity-testing lower bounds (Duchi–Ruan, Lam-Weil–Laurent–Loubes, Acharya et al., unified interactive lower bounds). Fix: in Related work, add a sentence for each, saying exactly what the private, causal setting adds beyond the known rate structure d²/(tL) and (log(e+d²L/t)/L)². Check that the Cerulli2026, Chen2025, Feng2026 and Xu2026 locators are accurate.

The welfare framing is under-argued. The paper says first-best welfare is 'a natural benchmark' but never explains why a practitioner would want minimax precision for V(P), rather than for the regret of a learned policy, in a trial with fixed fair assignment. The result is really a statement about private estimation of an ℓ1 norm of contrasts. Fix: open the introduction with a concrete reporting use case (e.g., the value of personalization, V−max-arm mean). Say plainly that the causal structure enters only through the signed-experiment reduction, which makes the welfare problem equivalent to the paired-TV problem on the symmetric family.

The interaction result is framed as a headline ('sequential adaptation improves … by at most a universal factor'), yet the constants are enormous (C_0/c is of order 10^{16} or more). Fix: say that rate-level equivalence is what is established, and drop or soften language implying practical equivalence of protocols.

Several 'definitions' (synth_3, synth_4, synth_5, synth_6) actually package theorem conclusions ('We say that … hold when …'). They duplicate content of \cref{obj:thm:uniform-private-value-frontiers,obj:thm:paired-uniform-tv-frontier}, which blurs what is defined and what is proved. Fix: delete these predicate-definitions. Keep the rate ρ in one definition and the paired procedure as a specialization of \cref{obj:def:frontier-handle}, and let the theorems carry all claims.
